Size of Cells
Smaller cell → higher surface area : volume ratio
Need more surface are to allow adequate nutrients to enter and waste to be expelled
explanation: A smaller cell maintains a higher surface area-to-volume ratio. This high ratio is crucial because cells need a relatively large surface area to allow adequate nutrients to enter and waste to be expelled efficiently relative to their internal volume.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the surface area-to-volume ratio of a smaller cell compared to a larger cell?
opts: A smaller cell has a lower surface area-to-volume ratio.
A smaller cell has a higher surface area-to-volume ratio.
A smaller cell has the same surface area-to-volume ratio.
Smaller cells do not have a surface area-to-volume ratio.
questions.exp: The slide explicitly states that a smaller cell has a 'higher surface area : volume ratio' to allow nutrients and wastes to transport efficiently.
